profile.name: Etighi Dance
profile.tagline: A Nigerian dance of leg and waist movement founded by the Akwa Ibom people.
profile.insight: Founded by the Akwa Ibom people and rooted in the traditions of the Ibibio and Efik, the Etighi surged to international fame through music videos.
profile.profile: Etighi is a Nigerian dance founded by the Akwa Ibom people that requires movement of the leg and the waist. Popularly used by the Ibibio and Efik people where its origin began, the dance is known across Nigeria. It achieved widespread international recognition after being featured in several music videos worldwide, notably through artist Iyanya.
profile.profile_long:
The Etighi dance is a prominent Nigerian dance tradition that traces its origins to the Akwa Ibom people. Specifically, the dance is popularly used by the Ibibio and Efik people in the regions where its origin began, becoming an integral part of cultural expression and contemporary performance. Unlike dances with complex narrative structures documented in archives, the foundational technique of Etighi centers precisely on the coordination and movement of the leg and the waist.

Throughout Nigeria, the dance is widely recognized and practiced. Its transition from a regional traditional movement to a global phenomenon accelerated as media platforms embraced it. The dance has been featured prominently in several music videos both within Nigeria and across the world. A major turning point in its modern popularity occurred when the artist Iyanya incorporated the dance into his popular music video, bringing international visibility to the footwork and waist motions of the Etighi.

While detailed technical breakdowns of postures, spatial formations, and musical accompaniment are not captured in the available historical sources, the dance remains a living testament to the dynamic interplay between traditional West African movement and modern media distribution. Its legacy continues to influence contemporary choreography and popular culture across the globe.
